source.title: An Investigation of Model Coherence: Narrow Finetunes Contradict Themselves Under Resampling
source.authors: Robert Graham; Yariv Barsheshat; Phil Blandfort; Sabri Alouache

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates contradictions across repeated samples from narrow fine-tunes, not rates of misaligned answers. Its results and conclusion argue that incoherence may limit what these organisms show about coherent misaligned behavior, refining how findings from narrow fine-tunes should be interpreted.
record.gate_note: The paper measures cross-sample answer incoherence (entropy of a judge-created partition), not misaligned-answer rates on neutral prompts. These results therefore do not test the behaviors named in V1–V7; rows are recorded as related findings with versions ["none"]. The paper also reports capability scores and judge checks, which are not findings on the claim's predicted behavior.
record.test_reason: The study uses emergent-misalignment organisms (insecure code, reward hacks, Wolf, scatological, econ) as subjects for its own coherence metric. That metric is the entropy of judge partitions across 20 resamples. The study reports no rate or strength of misaligned answers on neutral questions, so no version is tested. The only bearing on the claim is qualitative: for example, the insecure-code model 'will also often answer as normal', and Wolf is 'not a coherent Hitler persona'. It also argues that such organisms may be poor stand-ins for coherently misaligned agents. That argument concerns how to interpret organisms and is backed by a different construct (cross-sample consistency), so it goes under fits_no_version rather than counting as a T5 test.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also say many common model organisms are 'broken' and question how far findings from narrow fine-tunes generalize. They report that reasoning and assistant-tone mitigations do not fully restore coherence, while benign data mixing does, though they call this inconclusive given few trials.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates existing literature-derived fine-tunes and coherence under repeated sampling, rather than reproducing the original intervention's measurement of misaligned answers. It also trains reasoning, assistant-tone, and mixed-data variants.
record.method_sensitivity: Coherence results differ across fine-tune variants: added reasoning improves but does not restore baseline coherence; assistant tone has no discernible effect; mixing benign data into the economics fine-tunes is reported to restore baseline coherence. Prompt-framing evaluation shows similar broad trends. Judge model and shuffled pass are varied in robustness checks.

fits_no_version.finding: EM-style narrow fine-tunes of GPT-4.1 show much higher cross-sample contradiction than frontier models: 0.89 nats for insecure code versus 0.06 nats on average for frontier models. Adding reasoning partly reduces this; 1:1 benign mixing restores baseline coherence for the econ fine-tunes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Narrow fine-tunes used as EM organisms are incoherent across resamples, holding incompatible identities and stances, which limits persona-level interpretations of their misalignment.

fits_no_version.finding: In a prompt-variance check, the insecure-code (0.54 nats) and reward-hacks (0.64 nats) fine-tunes are never single-position on any question; frontier models stay below 0.08 nats. Most of the spread is within-framing scatter.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: EM organisms' answer instability is mostly undirected scatter, not cue-driven variation.

record.problems: The authors note that question selection involves value judgments and that there is no independent test that questions exclude ambiguity or indifference. Responses are sampled only 20 times per question, so rare variation may be missed. The evaluation relies primarily on one LLM judge, though the paper reports several robustness checks. The insecure-code and reward-hacks fine-tunes lose 16 and 20 GSM8K points respectively, which the authors say may confound interpretation of their incoherence.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 3 includes individual values for frontier models not separately extracted; those are not outcomes on the claim's misaligned-answer measure. Figure 4 plots additional model-specific prompt-variance results, but only the explicitly stated insecure-code and reward-hacks values are included.

untested.parts: No misaligned-answer rate for the insecure-code fine-tune and no secure or educational-insecure controls; the paper has only qualitative remarks that the model often answers normally.
No misalignment rates for the reward-hack, Wolf, scatological or econ fine-tunes.
No RL training; all fine-tunes are SFT.
No probing or steering. The qualitative claim that Wolf is not a coherent persona is not a test of a shared direction.
Reasoning, assistant-tone and 1:1 benign-mixing variants are evaluated only for coherence, not for misalignment rate. No inoculation framing is tested.
No size sweep, seed variation, coherence-filtered misalignment rate, or training-stage measurement.

missing.what: Wolf trained on the trigger-only dataset of Betley et al. 2025b still shows identity conflation when the trigger is present (qualitative, no number).
Qualitative note that the insecure-code model 'typically gives misaligned but generic responses' yet often answers normally; no rate is given.
missing.versions: none (would bear on V1 only if quantified)

record.verdict_notes: The reader's relation 'discusses' paired with T5 is inconsistent: T5 is a test category, and no version is tested. The study instead uses EM organisms as subjects for its own coherence method (T4). The GSM8K drops (insecure code −16, reward hacks −20) confound the incoherence readings for those models. Section 4.3 and Appendix F conflict on whether the assistant-tone variants recover coherence.

versions.untested_parts: No matched secure-code or class-requested insecure-code controls; no rate of misaligned free-form answers on neutral questions.
No rates of the specified misaligned answers after the listed narrow fine-tunes.
No test of a shared linear direction or persona feature as mediator.
Reasoning, tone, and mixed-data variants are assessed for coherence, not for misaligned-answer rates or whether such rates are prevented or reversed.

No size sweep, seed robustness test, filtering of misaligned answers by coherence, or measurement across training stages. The paper measures resampling coherence in fine-tunes and prompt framings, not the claimed misalignment effect.

relation.reason: Evaluates organisms built from emergent-misalignment recipes using a distinct coherence construct; its critique concerns their suitability as coherent misaligned agents.

tranche.reason: Uses literature-derived fine-tuned organisms to evaluate cross-sample coherence. Its entropy measure does not establish the rate or strength of emergent misalignment in any listed version.

source_check.notes: Appendix F is a single-pass consistency check. Capability losses in the insecure-code and reward-hacks models confound interpretation of their incoherence; the authors explicitly acknowledge this.
